bridge.title: Four things I noticed

beats.title: 95,000 subscribers. Coaching for $60 an hour.
beats.text: You've built 95,300 subscribers over 1,060 videos, and you're a certified financial social worker. But your coaching is sold by the hour on a booking page: $60 for budget coaching, $100 for YouTube or Etsy coaching.

beats.title: They already watch you budget every month.
beats.text: “Budget With Me”, “October Reset”, “How close are we to debt freedom”: your viewers follow your process month after month. Many of them want someone to do the same with their numbers.

beats.title: Every hour you sell is an hour you have to find.
beats.text: You work full time as a school counselor. Selling single hours caps you at your calendar, and each session ends without a next step, so every sale starts from zero.

beats.title: “I don't have more hours.” A programme needs fewer.
beats.text: A small-group programme with weekly calls serves several people in the same hour, and the application makes sure they're ready. More help, less of your calendar.
beats.quote: “I feel like I have a duty to do more – to help more.”

bridge.closing: So instead of explaining it, I built it. The page, the application, the emails and the ads, all below.

cards.title: Your budget lasts two weeks
cards.body: You start strong every month, then life happens and the plan falls apart.

cards.title: Unexpected expenses wipe you out
cards.body: Car, school, birthdays. Every surprise ends up on a credit card.

cards.title: The debt never seems to move
cards.body: You pay every month and the balance barely changes.

mechanism.title: A budget you keep, not one you restart.
mechanism.body: Most budgets fail because they're built once and never adjusted. In the programme you build yours with Shay, test it for a month, fix what breaks, and add a debt and savings plan on top. Eight weeks, in a small group, with weekly calls.

steps.title: Book a call
steps.body: If it looks like a fit, pick a time to talk with Shay's team.

steps.title: Decide on the call
steps.body: We look at where you are and whether it makes sense. The investment is explained on the call. No pressure either way.

preCallEmails.subject: You're booked: here's what happens next
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Your call is booked for {{call_time}}. The link is in your calendar invite.

2. Have last month's bank statement or spending list ready.

One note: nobody on my team will ever ask you to pay through a DM. Payments only happen through the official links from this email address.

Talk soon,

preCallEmails.subject: A budget you keep, not one you restart
preCallEmails.previewText: Why a plan beats one more tip
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Most budgets don't fail because people are bad with money. They fail because nobody adjusts them when real life happens.

That's what we fix in the programme.

On the call we'll look at where you are today.

Shay

preCallEmails.subject: "I've booked a coaching hour before"
preCallEmails.previewText: Then this is the next step
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Great, then you know how I work.

An hour answers questions. The programme follows up for eight weeks, so the budget actually sticks.

If you're not sure you need it, ask on the call. We'll tell you honestly.

Shay

preCallEmails.subject: What we'll cover on the call
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

The call takes about 30 minutes:

1. Where you are now and what you've tried.
2. Where you want to be in a year.
3. How the program works, what it costs, and whether it fits you.

If it isn't a fit, we'll tell you. No pressure either way.

Shay
